puzzles.description: Peer Unicorn is all about connection. Match each Malaysian state to its capital.

falseOutputs: Not quite — check which capital belongs to which state.
Try again. These aren't the obvious ones!

hints: Peer Unicorn is about connections — match each state to its capital.
Perak's is a former tin town. Pahang's sits at a river mouth. Negeri Sembilan's rhymes with 'ceramban'. Terengganu keeps the 'Kuala'.
Perak→Ipoh, Pahang→Kuantan, Negeri Sembilan→Seremban, Terengganu→Kuala Terengganu.

puzzles.description: Peer Unicorn celebrates people who bring the team together. Malaysia's national motto means 'Unity Is Strength' — spell its first word, the Malay word for 'united'.
hints: It's the first word of Malaysia's national motto 'Bersekutu Bertambah Mutu'.
Nine letters, starts with B, ends with U. Its root is 'sekutu' (ally/associate).

puzzles.description: Super Achiever reaches the top. How tall are the Petronas Twin Towers, in metres (rounded)?
hints: Super Achiever reaches the top — think of Malaysia's most famous towers.
The Petronas Twin Towers, rounded to the nearest metre. It's just over 451.

puzzles.description: Super Achiever is about record-breakers. Answer three about Malaysia's proudest feats.

questions.question: The Petronas Twin Towers held which world record?
Where does Merdeka 118 rank among the world's buildings today?
What was Malaysia's first national car?

hints: Think records and firsts — the towers once topped the whole world.
Petronas was #1 from 1998–2004; Merdeka 118 is #2 today; the first Proton shares a Scrabble-worthy name.

puzzles.description: Beyond Boundaries — Malaysian flavour that travels the world. Malaysia's national dish is 'nasi ____' — fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk. Spell the missing word (the Malay word for 'rich/fatty').
hints: The dish is 'nasi ____' — the missing word is the Malay word for 'rich' or 'fatty'.
Five letters, starts with L, ends with K.

puzzles.description: Mission control needs the facts straight — Malaysian nature edition. Tap TRUE or FALSE for each claim.

statements.text: Mount Kinabalu, Malaysia's highest peak, is located in Sarawak
The Malayan tapir is black and white in colour
The Rafflesia is famous for its pleasant, sweet fragrance

hints: Not all of these are true — read each claim carefully. Think about WHERE Kinabalu is, what a tapir looks like, and how a Rafflesia actually smells.
Mount Kinabalu is in Sabah, not Sarawak. The Malayan tapir really is black-and-white. The Rafflesia is nicknamed the 'corpse flower'.

puzzles.description: Set the date we celebrate tomorrow — the day Malaysia became Malaysia (DDMM).
hints: Careful — this is NOT Merdeka Day (31 August). That's when Malaya became independent.
Malaysia Day is in September — the 16th. Format is DDMM.
